title: Times Tables to 15
subtitle: Factors 0 to 15
bounds: Factors 0 to 15. Forms: R a × b = ?, C a × ? = p, S ? × b = p (a missing factor is never 0). T1 R: the easy rows (0, 1, 2, 5, 10) and 11 times a digit, at least 12 with a factor of 11 to 15 (147 prompts); T2 R: a factor of 11-15 times 3 or 4, not an easy fact (at least 12; 43 prompts with the 3-4-9 core); T3 R: a factor of 11-15 times 6-15, not an easy fact (at least 12), else a 6, 7 or 8 core fact (84); T4 C: hard facts with a factor of 11-15 (at least 12), else any hard fact with factors 3-15 (109); T5 S: hard facts with a factor of 11-15 (at least 8), any hard fact (at least 4), plus C (at least 4 with 11-15; 218 prompts in all). At most 6 prompts per tier with a 0 factor. Wrong choices are distinct non-negative whole numbers up to 999. R: at least two within the larger factor of the answer (at least 2), at most one far; with a factor of 11 or more and an answer of 20 or more, one wrong value shares the answer's ones digit. C and S: at least two within 2 of the answer, at most one far. Answer ranks (smallest to largest of the four) each hold 15 to 35 percent of a tier.

tiers.name: Easy rows to 15
tiers.description: Times 0, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 11, with factors up to 15.

tiers.name: Teens times 3 and 4
tiers.description: Factors 11 to 15 times 3 and 4. Split into tens and ones.

tiers.name: Teens times 6 to 15
tiers.description: Factors 11 to 15 times 6 and up. Split a factor, then add.

tiers.name: Missing factors
tiers.description: Missing factor: 14 × ? = 98. Ask what times 14 makes 98.

tiers.name: Missing first factors
tiers.description: First factor missing: ? × 14 = 98, or a missing second factor. Factors up to 15.

GROUP_OFF.student: One group too many or too few. Count the groups, then the size of each.
GROUP_OFF.teacher: Off by one group: a × (b + 1), a × (b − 1), (a + 1) × b or (a − 1) × b.

ADDED.student: × means equal groups, not +. 4 × 3 is 4 groups of 3, which is 12.
ADDED.teacher: Adds the factors instead of multiplying: 4 × 3 = 7.

DROPPED_CARRY.student: Keep the ten: 13 × 6 is 60 + 18, and the 18 has a ten to add in.
DROPPED_CARRY.teacher: Splits into tens and ones but loses the ten from the ones product: 13 × 6 = 60 + 8 = 68.

TENS_SLIP.student: Check the tens place. Split into tens and ones, multiply each, add both.
TENS_SLIP.teacher: Right ones digit, tens place off by one ten (product plus or minus 10).

PARTIAL_PRODUCTS.student: Tens × tens plus ones × ones skips two parts. Split one number, multiply both.
PARTIAL_PRODUCTS.teacher: Multiplies tens by tens and ones by ones only: 13 × 14 = 100 + 12 = 112.

MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Check it: multiply your number by the shown one. Does it make the total?
MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing factor one too high or too low: counted the groups wrong, or never multiplied back to check.

MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Not subtraction. Ask: this number times what makes the total?
MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the shown factor from the product (p − k) instead of dividing the product by it.

MISSING_PRODUCT.student: The total is the product, not the missing factor. Multiply back to check.
MISSING_PRODUCT.teacher: Writes the product as the missing factor: the number already given in the equation.
